ref: DAR — Revelation ch. 2: The Seven Churches
title: The Seven Churches
voicePrompt: Explain in your own words why Uriah Smith reads the messages to the seven churches as prophetic of successive periods of church history rather than only letters to literal first-century congregations. Walk through how he applies the first four churches — Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, and Thyatira — to specific eras.

questions.stem: According to the chapter, how should the messages to the seven churches be understood?
options: As prophetic of seven distinct periods covering the Christian age
As letters meant only for seven literal congregations in Asia
As an allegory of seven spiritual gifts of the Holy Spirit
As a record of seven councils held by the early church
questions.explanation: The chapter argues the messages to the seven churches should be regarded as prophetic, 'having their application to seven distinct periods covering the Christian age,' citing Vitringa, Gill, and others who held this view.

questions.stem: What does the chapter say 'the angel' of each church denotes?
options: A literal angelic guardian assigned to each congregation
The messenger or ministry — all the true ministers of Christ during that period
A symbol of the Holy Spirit speaking to the church
The bishop of Rome ruling over the churches
questions.explanation: The chapter states the angel of a church 'must denote a messenger, or minister,' and since each church covers a period of time, 'the angel of each church must denote the ministry, or all the true ministers of Christ during the period covered by that church.'

questions.stem: How does the chapter explain Christ's threat to 'remove thy candlestick out of his place' from Ephesus, given that the period would end regardless of repentance?
options: The candlestick is removed automatically when each church period expires
The threat applies only to the literal city of Ephesus, not to later periods
Removing the candlestick means taking away gospel privileges they could still enjoy — a rejection by Christ — which is not the same as a period merely expiring
The threat was never carried out because Ephesus repented
questions.explanation: The chapter answers that 'the expiration of the period covered by any church is not the removal of the candlestick of that church.' Removal would take away privileges they 'might and should longer enjoy,' a rejection by Christ as his light-bearers, applicable to individuals as well as the church.

questions.stem: How does the chapter interpret the 'tribulation ten days' promised to the church of Smyrna?
options: Ten literal days of persecution in the city of Smyrna
Ten prophetic days meaning ten years, fulfilled in the Diocletian persecution from A.D. 302 to 312
Ten separate empires that would oppress the church
Ten generations of faithful martyrs
questions.explanation: Because the message is prophetic, the chapter holds the time must also be prophetic, denoting ten years, and notes 'the last and most bloody of the ten persecutions continued just ten years, under Diocletian, from A. D. 302 to A. D. 312.'

questions.stem: According to William Miller as quoted in the chapter, what does the name 'Antipas' (in the Pergamos message) most likely refer to?
options: A single faithful martyr named Antipas described in ancient histories
The apostle John writing under a pseudonym
A class of men who opposed the power of the bishops or popes — anti (against) plus papas (pope)
The city where Satan's seat was located
questions.explanation: Miller is quoted saying Antipas was 'not an individual, but a class of men who opposed the power of the bishops, or popes,' being a combination of 'anti, opposed, and papas, father, or pope,' since history is 'perfectly silent respecting such an individual.'

questions.stem: What period does the chapter assign to the church of Thyatira, and why?
options: The apostolic age, from Christ's resurrection to A.D. 100
The days of Constantine, A.D. 323 to 538
A.D. 538 to 1798 — the 1260 years of papal supremacy
A.D. 1798 to the second advent
questions.explanation: Since Pergamos terminates with the setting up of the papacy in A.D. 538, the chapter assigns Thyatira to 'the continuance of this blasphemous power, through the 1260 years of its supremacy, or from A. D. 538 to A. D. 1798.'

questions.stem: What distinguishes Christ's command 'Hold fast till I come' to Thyatira from the comings threatened to Ephesus and Pergamos?
options: It is a conditional threat of judgment if they do not repent
It is an unconditional coming — the future second advent set before believers as a matter of hope
It refers to a figurative removal of their candlestick
It refers to Christ fighting them with the sword of his mouth
questions.explanation: The chapter contrasts the conditional 'Repent, or else I will come' threats to Ephesus and Pergamos with Thyatira's 'unconditional coming,' which is 'suspended upon no conditions' and 'can refer to no other event but the future second advent of the Lord in glory.'

questions.stem: Why does the chapter say many modern commentators discarded the prophetic view of the seven churches?
options: Because of the comparatively recent and unscriptural doctrine of the temporal millennium
Because the original Greek manuscripts had been lost
Because the church of Laodicea no longer existed
Because the apostle John denied the messages were prophetic
questions.explanation: The chapter states what led commentators to discard the prophetic view 'is the comparatively recent and unscriptural doctrine of the temporal millennium,' since the last church's state seemed incompatible with a thousand years of a converted world.
